title: Output probability and nontermination bound
statement: Let $r$ be a function from finite Boolean words to either an output in a set $\alpha$ or no output, and suppose that once $r$ outputs a value, appending any Boolean word leaves that output unchanged. For any output $v\in\alpha$ and natural numbers $t,t'$, the probability that $r$ outputs $v$ on a uniformly random Boolean word of length $t'$ is at most the probability that it outputs $v$ on a uniformly random Boolean word of length $t$, plus the probability that it has not halted on a uniformly random Boolean word of length $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $r$ is prefix-stable: an output persists after appending any word
